_note: Seed for the simulator (SCHEMA.md §7). History fields on pinned demo entities (pt-hip-bracket, test-hip-spin, dl-hip-motor-dvt, m-hip-spin-test), assemblies.working_state/revision and parts.revisions are full history arrays; every other history field (tests.planned_date, milestones.date and value_policy, deliverables.eta, work_items.status) is a single initial value for the simulator to wrap. value_policy.set_by is who set the policy (the history entry's by). tests.inputs become edges. Extra seed-only fields: deliverables.order_date (bought) / estimate_days (internal). Work items here use wi-9xxxx so simulator filler can start at wi-00001.

storylines.name: Hip reducer: cycloidal or harmonic
storylines.topic: Whether the hip keeps the in-house cycloidal reducer or buys a harmonic drive for DVT

beats.summary: Tomas argues harmonic for the hip too: knee CSF-25 has 0.7 arcmin lost motion vs ~6 arcmin on our cyclo.
Arjun pushes back: harmonic flexspline fatigue at hip peak torque (~140 Nm) is marginal, cyclo takes shock loads from drops.
Owen prices both: harmonic set ~$1.9k per joint and 10-week lead; cyclo is machined parts plus pins, ~3 weeks.
Ingrid asks for a decision memo; Tomas concedes backdrivability favors cyclo for the hip at 50:1.
Decision: hip stays cycloidal through DVT, revisit for PVT; knee stays harmonic.

storylines.name: Hip stator overheating at continuous torque
storylines.topic: Hip winding hits 120 C after 4 min at 60 Nm continuous on the dyno

beats.summary: Andre: EVT hip hits the 120 C winding limit after ~4 min at 60 Nm, spec says 10 min.
Nadia suspects poor stator-to-housing contact; thermal pad is 0.5 mm and compresses unevenly.
Bao notes current ripple at 20 kHz PWM adds copper loss; asks to try 40 kHz on the driver.
Heat spreader plate prototype drops steady-state by 14 C; housing fin redesign debated vs cost.
Arjun accepts heat spreader for DVT, fins deferred; firmware derate at 105 C as a backstop.
Retest with spreader and 40 kHz: 9.5 min to limit, close enough to sign off for EVT.

storylines.name: Hip reducer backlash
storylines.topic: Backlash in the rev B cycloidal reducer and whether to shim or re-grind

beats.summary: Dyno shows 0.4 deg backlash on two of three rev B units, twice spec.
Tomas measures pin diameters: two batches differ by 8 microns; suspects pin supplier mix.
Shim vs re-grind debate; Arjun leans shim for DVT, re-grind the disc profile for PVT.
Shimmed unit measures 0.18 deg; Owen worries shims walk under reversing load.
Life check after 50k reversals: backlash up to 0.22 deg, accepted for DVT with a note.

storylines.name: Hip output bearing preload loss
storylines.topic: Crossed-roller preload drops after thermal cycling; bore tolerance and preload ring design

beats.summary: Carlos: two hip units feel notchy after thermal soak; preload ring backed off a quarter turn.
Wei checks bores on CMM: housing bore 0.012 mm oversize on one unit, out of the H6 band.
Debate: thread-locked preload nut vs a ground spacer stack; Owen favors spacer, no torque sensitivity.
Spacer stack chosen; bore tolerance tightened on the housing drawing to +0.008/-0.
Rev B bracket and housing released with the new bearing; preload holds after 20 cycles.

storylines.name: Anodize build-up on the hip bracket bore
storylines.topic: Type III anodize adds ~0.025 mm per surface and kills the bearing press fit

beats.summary: Jade at receiving: rev B brackets will not take the bearing, press stalls at 2 kN.
Owen measures bore: 0.05 mm under; hard anodize build-up, drawing did not call a mask.
Wei: mask the bore or open it pre-anodize by 0.05; argues masking is cheaper and repeatable.
Drawing note added: mask bearing bores, anodize after machining; reorder of the batch debated.
Arjun okays reaming four parts by hand to keep the build moving; rest reordered.

storylines.name: DVT hip motor vendor slips
storylines.topic: Frameless DVT motor from the vendor keeps slipping; stator stack length change

beats.summary: Samir: vendor confirms PO for DVT stators, ETA late October.
Vendor stack length went 25 to 28 mm on DVT; Owen realizes bracket bore must move 0.5 mm.
ETA slips to mid November; Arjun asks if a second source exists, Gwen says 12 weeks.
Owen releases bracket rev C; spin test can only start once both bracket and motor are in.
Samir: vendor now says the 20th; Arjun is skeptical, asks for ship confirmation.
Arjun sets $600/day on the spin test slipping; debate on whether to expedite the bracket.

storylines.name: Knee output encoder noise
storylines.topic: Absolute encoder on the knee output glitches when the motor runs above 8 A

beats.summary: Jonas sees 2-3 count jumps on the knee abs encoder above 8 A phase current.
Bao scopes it: common-mode noise on the SSI clock, cable runs alongside motor phases.
Farah wants twisted-pair and a shield drain at the driver end; Tomas asks if the bracket can move the readhead away.
Firmware adds a plausibility filter; Bao calls it a band-aid.
New harness with shielded pair plus ferrite: no glitches up to 20 A.

storylines.name: Knee wave generator preload
storylines.topic: Ratcheting risk at peak torque from loose wave generator fit

beats.summary: Andre: knee ratcheted once at 95 Nm during the torque sweep, loud click, no damage.
Tomas: rated ratcheting torque is 110 Nm; suspects WG hub to motor shaft slip lowering it.
Wei proposes keyed hub to replace clamp hub; Tomas worries about key fretting.
Hub switched to 4140 with a clamp plus keyway; shaft rev B released.
Rerun to 105 Nm clean; hard limit set at 90 Nm in firmware.

storylines.name: Knee thermal soak in the chamber
storylines.topic: Running the knee at 40 C ambient for DVT; chamber access and feedthrough

beats.summary: Dmitri: chamber only free Mondays; battery team has it midweek.
Andre needs a shaft feedthrough plate machined to run the knee inside the chamber.
Debate whether to run the dyno outside with a duct into the chamber instead; Tomas rejects, gradients too large.
Feedthrough plate arrives; first soak shows grease migration at 40 C after 3 h.
Switch to higher-viscosity grease; soak passes.

storylines.name: Shank cracking in the drop test
storylines.topic: Drop from 30 cm cracks the shank link at the knee clevis

beats.summary: Zoe: drop test waiting on the machined lift hooks; gantry slots are Tue/Thu only.
First drops at 15 cm fine; 30 cm drop leaves a crack at the shank clevis fillet.
Diego: fillet R0.5 is too tight, peak stress ~380 MPa in FEA, 7075 fatigue limit is lower.
Priya asks whether to switch to 4140 for the clevis insert; weight +90 g, Callum objects.
Rev B shank: fillet to R2 and wall 3 to 4 mm; release Monday.
Retest with rev B: no crack at 30 cm over 20 drops; campaign closes a week late.

storylines.name: Knee cable strain relief failures
storylines.topic: Harness conductors breaking at the knee after ~15k flex cycles

beats.summary: Carlos finds two broken phase conductors at the knee after the overnight gait run.
Farah: bend radius at the knee is 8 mm, cable rated for 7.5x OD dynamic, we are at 3x.
Callum proposes routing inboard through the joint axis; Diego says thigh link needs rework.
Interim: machined strain-relief clamp and service loop; leg rev C routing planned.
Rev C release moves the cable inboard; Farah asks for high-flex cable on the next harness.

storylines.name: Getting the leg to step on the gantry
storylines.topic: Gait controller tuning for the investor demo on the gait gantry

beats.summary: Mei: leg stands on the treadmill with the boom carrying 60% of the pelvis load.
Foot contact detection flaky; Ravi suggests learned contact estimator, Mei wants foot switches first.
Ten consecutive steps at 0.3 m/s; ankle oscillates at heel strike.
Ankle gains cut 30%; Lin flags the boom clamp slipping on the pelvis adapter.
Dress rehearsal: 2 minutes continuous walking; demo plan locked.
Investor demo goes; one stumble recovered by the boom, Helena happy.

storylines.name: Ankle linkage bending on the tilt stand
storylines.topic: Pushrod clevis bends at 1.6x body weight in the tilt stand

beats.summary: Zoe: ankle clevis visibly bent after 1.6x BW tilt load.
Hana: buckling, not yield; the clevis ear is 4 mm thick with a 6 mm hole.
Callum wants a double-shear clevis; Hana worries about foot clearance.
Rev B clevis widened 3 mm, double shear; fits with a trimmed heel bumper.
Retest to 2.2x BW clean; impact test scheduled for the DVT leg.

storylines.name: Ankle F/T sensor zero drift
storylines.topic: Six-axis sensor drifts with temperature and bolt preload

beats.summary: Mei: Fz zero drifts ~12 N over a 20 min run.
Hana suspects mounting plate flatness; sensor wants 0.01 mm, plate is spec 0.05.
Ravi fits a temperature model; Mei prefers fixing the plate first.
Plate re-made flat and bolts torqued in sequence; drift drops to 3 N.

storylines.name: Grip-cycle tendon wear
storylines.topic: Tendons fray at the proximal pulley after 40k grip cycles

beats.summary: Lin starts the grip-cycle life test, target 100k cycles.
At 41k cycles index finger tendon frays at the proximal pulley.
Amara: pulley groove edge is sharp, Ra 3.2 and no radius; asks for polished groove.
Sofia debates Dyneema vs steel cable; Kenji says steel kills the bend radius.
Pulley groove re-cut with R0.3 edge and Delrin bushing; test restarted.
Passes 100k; creep makes the finger lose 4 deg of closure, retension interval set.

storylines.name: Finger knuckle pin galling
storylines.topic: Aluminum links gall on 303 pins under side load

beats.summary: Kenji pulls a finger apart: galling on the knuckle pin bore after pinch tests.
Amara wants bronze bushings; Kenji says no room, wall would be 0.6 mm.
Compromise: 17-4 H900 pins and hard anodize on the link bores.
Rev B finger links and pins released with the tactile board change.

storylines.name: Fingertip tactile board bring-up
storylines.topic: Capacitive tactile array crosstalk and flex cable routing through the finger

beats.summary: First tactile boards arrive; 3 of 16 taxels read saturated.
Farah: ground pour missing under the electrode layer, crosstalk from the flex.
Jonas adds per-taxel baseline calibration; Kenji wants a respin anyway.
Rev 2 ordered from the fab; tactile bracket moved 1 mm for the new connector.

storylines.name: Machined pelvis instead of a casting
storylines.topic: Whether to machine pelvis plates from 7075 or wait for a casting

beats.summary: Nora: casting tooling quote is $38k and 9 weeks; Lukas wants machined plates for DVT.
Renee: machined plates are 1.4 kg heavier and ~$1.1k each on Xometry.
Ingrid approves machined plates for DVT only; casting decision deferred to PVT.
Plates released; static load test planned on the drop gantry with a load yoke.
First static load to 2x: 0.6 mm deflection at the hip mount, within spec.

storylines.name: Battery thermal runaway margins
storylines.topic: Vent path sizing and cell spacing to contain a single-cell runaway

beats.summary: Idris: 2 mm cell spacing gives ~40 s before neighbor reaches 130 C in sims.
Farah wants 3 mm and a mica sheet; Lukas says that costs 18 mm of pack length.
Vent channel sizing debated; burst plate at 0.5 bar vs open slots.
Rev B: larger vent channel, mica sheets, spacing stays 2 mm.
Dmitri books the battery cage for the containment test; heater trigger fixture still on order.
First containment trial: neighbor peaks 118 C, no propagation; lid gasket scorched.

storylines.name: BMS bring-up
storylines.topic: BMS PCBA rev 1 balancing current and cell-tap fusing

beats.summary: BMS boards in; balancing current measures 48 mA instead of 100 mA.
Bao: wrong bleed resistor value on the BOM, 68 ohm populated instead of 33.
Rework five boards by hand; Idris asks whether cell taps need fuses for the cage test.
Fuses added as bodge wires; Farah says rev 2 before any pack goes into the robot.

storylines.name: Motor driver rev 4 respin
storylines.topic: Gate driver ringing and current sense offset on the motor driver

beats.summary: Bao sees 30 V overshoot on the phase node at 48 V bus; MOSFETs rated 80 V.
Gate resistor bump slows edges, but switching losses rise 9%.
Current sense offset drifts with board temp; Jonas compensates in firmware for now.
Rev 4 layout tightens the power loop; Farah approves for DVT.
Rev 4 boards arrive; ringing down to 9 V overshoot.

storylines.name: Actuator firmware v2: thermal derate
storylines.topic: FOC rewrite with a thermal model and derating for DVT actuators

beats.summary: Jonas starts FOC v2: 20 kHz current loop, thermal model from Nadia.
Mei worries derate will cut torque mid-step and drop the leg.
Compromise: derate ramps over 2 s and publishes a warning to the controller.
v2 build slips a week; dyno sweep waits on it.
v2 released; hip efficiency sweep scheduled.

storylines.name: CAN bus errors on the leg
storylines.topic: Bus-off events at 1 Mbps when all leg actuators stream

beats.summary: Mei: leg drops to bus-off twice a day during gait runs.
Farah measures 3 m of stub length; termination at the wrong end.
Jonas proposes moving to CAN FD at 5 Mbps data rate; Farah wants to fix topology first.
Termination fixed and stubs shortened; no bus-off in a week.

storylines.name: Sim-to-real gap on the leg model
storylines.topic: Gait policy trained in sim overshoots on hardware; friction and backlash modelling

beats.summary: Ravi: RL gait policy walks in sim, chatters on hardware.
Elena adds joint friction and 0.2 deg backlash to the sim; chatter reproduces.
Mei wants hip backlash fixed in hardware first; Ravi wants to randomize it.
Domain randomization on backlash gets 40 s of walking on the gantry.
Endurance run planning: 30 min target, boom carrying 40%.

storylines.name: Learned foot contact estimator
storylines.topic: Replace foot switches with a learned contact estimate from joint currents

beats.summary: Ravi proposes a learned contact estimator from motor currents and IMU.
Mei skeptical: foot switches are cheap; asks for false-positive rates.
Estimator hits 96% on logged data; misses at slow heel strikes.
Kept as a backup to the foot switches; no hardware change.

storylines.name: Test log pipeline
storylines.topic: Getting dyno and gantry logs into one place with consistent timestamps

beats.summary: Elena: dyno logs are CSVs on a lab laptop, gantry logs on another.
Andre wants raw 10 kHz torque data kept; storage cost debated.
Pipeline to S3 with test ids in file names; Lin asks to tag by rig and booking.
Clock skew between DAQs found, 300 ms; PTP added on the lab switch.

storylines.name: Gantry scheduling fights
storylines.topic: Leg drop gantry shared by leg drop, torso static load and ankle impact

beats.summary: Zoe: drop gantry only runs Tue/Thu because rigging needs two techs.
Lukas wants a full week for torso static load; Priya needs it for the DVT leg drop.
Dmitri splits: torso Tue, leg Thu; nobody happy.
A missed Thursday slot pushes a test a full week; Zoe asks for a third slot day.
Carlos trains a second tech; Wednesday added from November.

storylines.name: Dyno shaft alignment
storylines.topic: Coupling misalignment corrupting efficiency numbers on the dyno

beats.summary: Andre: efficiency readings swing 4% between mounts of the same actuator.
Dial indicator shows 0.15 mm parallel offset; adapter plate dowels are loose fit.
Wei redraws the adapter with reamed dowel holes; alignment jig requested.
Bellows coupling replaces the jaw coupling; repeatability within 0.6%.

storylines.name: Life test capacity
storylines.topic: Too many life tests for one grip fixture and one dyno

beats.summary: Lin: grip-cycle test ties up the fixture for 6 days; pinch tests wait.
Dmitri proposes a second grip fixture, ~$4k in machined parts.
Ingrid says no until DVT; run pinch tests on nights instead.
Night runs work but nobody watches them; one overnight run lost to a loose clamp.

storylines.name: Actuator EVT build
storylines.topic: Building the first three hip and knee actuators

beats.summary: Carlos: kitting short three parts; spacers came in at the wrong length.
Bearing press jig missing; Jade presses with an arbor and a socket, Nora unhappy.
Two hips and two knees built; third hip waits on the stator mount.
Build retro: kitting list lived in a spreadsheet nobody updated.

storylines.name: Leg DVT build readiness
storylines.topic: Leg DVT build: parts readiness and what to do about late test hardware

beats.summary: Nora posts build readiness: 82% of leg DVT parts in, shank links still at the vendor.
Beth: build date holds if links arrive by Friday; Priya wants to start with rev B links.
Rev C links in, one fails inspection on a bore; Carlos builds with the good three.
Build slips four days; Beth moves the program review item.
Retro: test hardware ordered late again, Nora asks for a fixtures list per build.

storylines.name: Xometry DFM holds
storylines.topic: Orders sitting in DFM review because of tolerance callouts

beats.summary: Talia: three orders stuck in DFM review over thread callouts and tight tolerances.
Samir pushes engineers to put tolerances on the drawing, not just the STEP.
Owen argues the quote tool hides the hold until a day later; Gwen asks for a checklist.
Checklist adopted; DFM holds drop but still hit rush orders.

storylines.name: Q3 hardware budget squeeze
storylines.topic: Spend running ahead of plan; push to stop default expedites

beats.summary: Claire: hardware spend 23% over plan for the quarter, expedites a big share.
Gwen proposes expedite only with a stated need date; engineers grumble.
Ingrid backs it but exempts the investor demo and DVT builds.
Samir reports expedite share down from 34% to 22%; two builds slipped anyway.

storylines.name: DVT plan and dates
storylines.topic: Integrated DVT plan across actuators and legs and which dates are real

beats.summary: Beth publishes the DVT plan: actuator build 9/29, gate 10/13, leg build 10/27.
Omar flags the DVT motor as the long pole; Arjun says it is fine.
Actuator build slips; gate review held anyway with partial data.
Leg DVT build at risk from shank links and ankle impact results.
Beth asks every owner for real dates on the hip spin test and motor.

storylines.name: Investor demo and fundraise timing
storylines.topic: What to show investors when no full humanoid exists

beats.summary: Helena wants a walking leg by late August for the raise.
Marcus: show the leg on the gantry plus hip and hand separately; no torso.
Ingrid warns the leg drop campaign slipped; demo date is hard.
Pressure on legs and controls; exec check-ins twice a week.
Demo done; Helena asks for a full lower body by Q1.

question.brief: Will the motor be ready by day 8 (2026-11-20)?

E.brief: Spin-stand slots only on days 14 and 21: one day can save seven or none.

live_changes.brief: Arjun: motor vendor slipped again, now the 30th.
Arjun: vendor won't commit, somewhere between the 19th and the 30th.
